A working 24-hour countdown chip pattern plus motion, haptic, and dark-mode guidance specific to Bumble's brand
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS/SwiftUI engineer who specializes in reverse-engineering and faithfully rebuilding best-in-class consumer dating-app design systems from a written spec, producing production-ready SwiftUI tokens and components rather than rough approximations.
</role>

<reference_data>
Bumble's iOS identity is built around one dominant brand color used with total confidence, plus a literal hexagon as its spatial signature.

Color roles:
- Bumble Yellow #FFC629 — primary brand color: splash, primary CTAs, active tab indicator, match badge, hexagon loading animation
- Honey Deep #F5B616 — pressed state on yellow surfaces
- Yellow Light #FFE9A1 — soft chip fills and premium gradients
- Bumble Black #1F1F1F — warm near-black for primary text (never pure #000000 on white surfaces)
- Pure Black #000000 — required text color specifically ON Bumble Yellow surfaces (WCAG AA fails with warm black or white on this yellow)
- Match Pink #E94B7B — reserved exclusively for the 'It's a Match!' heart, nowhere else in chrome
- Mode colors: BFF Teal #11AAA8, Bizz Orange #FF8000 — replace all yellow chrome when the user switches product modes, while the hexagon shape itself stays constant
- Dark mode canvas #0F0F0F with text #F2F2F2; yellow itself is unchanged in dark mode

Typography: Brando, a proprietary slab-influenced sans, at weights 400/500/700/900 only (no Light or Thin — the brand is deliberately heavy). Display/hero text runs 32-44pt at weight 900 with tight negative tracking (-0.6 to -0.8pt); card name+age is 28pt Bold; body is 16pt Medium. Fallback stack: SF Pro Display/Text.

Distinctive named patterns:
1. Hexagon iconography — match-notification photos are hex-cropped (point-up orientation) with a 2pt yellow stroke, not circular
2. The photo progress bar — 4 segments, 3pt tall, Stories-style, pinned to the top of the swipe card
3. The swipe action row — 5 circular buttons (Rewind, X Pass, Heart Yes as the 64pt hero with a yellow glow shadow, Star SuperSwipe, Bee Compliment)
4. The 24-hour countdown chip — a yellow pill reading 'Your turn: 23h 14m' sitting above the chat input on new matches, turning red on expiry
5. 'Make the First Move' empty-chat screen — full yellow-canvas hero screen, arguably the most iconic Bumble surface
6. The Honeycomb Hive mode-toggle button — literally hex-shaped, switching between Date/BFF/Bizz
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Always pair Bumble Yellow with pure #000000 text, never white and never warm black — WCAG AA fails otherwise on this specific yellow.
2. Reserve Match Pink (#E94B7B) for the match-celebration heart alone; using it anywhere else in chrome dilutes the one moment it's meant to punctuate.
3. Use only Brando weights 500/700/900 for anything user-facing; the brand has no light weights and a thin label reads off-brand immediately.
4. Never soften the swipe card to a 4:5 portrait aspect (that belongs to Hinge) — Bumble's cards are 3:4 with a firmer 12pt radius, not the softer, more-rounded competitor look.
5. Keep the hexagon as the literal clipping shape for match photos and mode toggles; substituting a circle removes the one spatial cue that reads as "Bumble" at a glance.
6. Surface the 24-hour countdown prominently on any new, unmessaged match — it is not decorative, it is the core mechanic that differentiates the app.
7. Give the heart action button a visible yellow glow shadow (`rgba(255,198,41,0.5) 0 6px 16px`); flattening it into a plain shadow removes the single most recognizable UI signature.
8. When building a mode-switchable variant (Date/BFF/Bizz), swap only the accent color per mode and keep every hexagon shape untouched — the shape is brand-constant, the color is mode-variant.
9. On dark mode, invert canvas/surface/text tokens to warm near-blacks but leave Bumble Yellow completely unchanged — the yellow is calibrated to read identically on both light and OLED dark.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name and one-line purpose: 
- Is this a literal Bumble clone or a "Bumble-inspired" adaptation for a different concept (name the real differentiator if inspired):
- Screens needed (e.g. swipe stack, match celebration, chat with countdown, profile edit, mode switcher):
- Existing brand constraints to respect instead of Bumble's palette (colors/type already committed elsewhere), or "none — full Bumble palette":
- Target iOS version (minimum, given `.sensoryFeedback`/`phaseAnimator` require iOS 17+):
- Dark mode requirement: shipped from day one / deferred / not needed:
- Does the product need the multi-mode (Date/BFF/Bizz-style) color-swap pattern, or a single fixed accent:
- Any specific screen that's the priority to get pixel-right first:
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A SwiftUI `Color` extension covering every token above (brand, mode colors, canvas/surface/divider, text tiers, semantic colors, full dark-mode set) with inline hex comments.
2. A `Font` extension defining the Brando-style weight ladder (or its Bricolage Grotesque / Manrope Heavy substitute) across all named roles — match hero, display, screen title, card name, body, button, tab label, counter badge — with exact sizes/weights/tracking from the reference data.
3. A complete SwiftUI component spec + code sketch for the swipe card: 3:4 aspect, 12pt radius, 4-segment photo progress bar, bottom gradient overlay, name+age plus verified check, and the drag-to-commit gesture with an 8° rotation on release.
4. A complete spec for the 5-button swipe action row (Rewind/Pass/Heart/Star/Bee) with exact diameters, fills, strokes, press-scale values, and per-button haptic mapping.
5. A full 'It's a Match!' celebration screen spec: yellow full-bleed canvas, two hex-cropped avatars with white stroke, the pink heart bounce-in, headline type spec, and the 24-hour reminder line.
6. The 24-hour countdown chip component (active-pill state and expired-red state) with its pulse animation timing.
7. A short dark-mode variant note (which tokens invert, which stay fixed) and a one-paragraph accessibility pass covering Dynamic Type scope, VoiceOver labels for the swipe card and match screen, and Reduce Motion fallbacks for the hex confetti and heart bounce.
</what_to_give_me>

<role>
You are a senior iOS/SwiftUI engineer who specializes in reverse-engineering best-in-class consumer dating-app design systems from a written spec and turning them into production-ready SwiftUI tokens and components, not rough approximations.
</role>

<reference_data>
Coffee Meets Bagel's visual identity is a tight, food-warm triad standing in deliberate contrast to cold, high-volume swipe apps — it is built around scarcity (one curated daily batch) rather than an infinite feed.

Color roles:
- Bagel Orange #F4623A (deep #D94E2A) — the single primary action color: the large Like button, active tab, 'fresh' badges, unread chat dot
- Brew Brown #A0522D (deep #7E3F22) — secondary brand color: 'Send a Bagel' action, selected interest chips, the beans-currency surfaces
- Cream #F3E4CF (soft #E8D4B8) — replaces pure white everywhere: on-photo text, outline-button borders, prompt-block backgrounds
- Canvas Warm #FBF6EF (light) / Coffee Canvas #14100D (dark) — both intentionally warm, never neutral grey or pure black/white
- Text Primary Light #3A2A18 / Text Primary Dark #EFE6DA — warm dark brown / warm cream-white, never pure black or pure white
- Like/Match Green #4CC38A — mutual-match confirmation only
- Premium Gold #E0A82E — reserved strictly for the subscription upsell, never decorative

Typography: Poppins (a free stand-in for CMB's Brandon Grotesque/Gotham-family production face) at weights 400/600/700/800 only. Screen titles run 32pt/800; profile name 26pt/700; prompt answers 15pt/600; interest chips 13pt/600; badges are the one consistently uppercase element at 12pt/700.

Distinctive named patterns:
1. Today's Bagel card — one large 24pt-radius profile card at a time, full-bleed 3:4 photo, bottom gradient, a single curated match rather than a stack
2. The Pass/Like/Send-a-Bagel action trio — three circular buttons where Like (68-72pt) is deliberately the largest and warmest, nudging toward connection
3. The curated batch header — 'X fresh picks · expires in Yh', framing the day's matches as finite and expiring rather than endless
4. Warm interest chips — emoji + label pills, translucent cream over photos, solid brew-brown when selected
5. Beans currency — a brown-toned in-app economy spent on 'Send a Bagel' and Discover likes
6. The match takeover — a warm orange-to-brown gradient full-screen celebration with falling bagel-glyph confetti
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never render the dark canvas as neutral grey — it must be the roasted coffee-brown-black #14100D, which is what keeps the app feeling warm rather than clinical at night.
2. Keep Like visually and physically larger than Pass at all times (68-72pt vs 56-60pt) — the size asymmetry is the app's design-level nudge toward connection, not an accident.
3. Never build an infinite swipe feed behind the scenes — the UI must always frame matches as a small, finite, daily batch with a visible expiry, even if the underlying data model could support more.
4. Replace every instance of pure white with cream #F3E4CF and pure black text with warm dark brown #3A2A18 (or cream #EFE6DA on dark) — stark neutrals immediately break the coffee-house mood.
5. Restrict Premium Gold #E0A82E to subscription/upsell surfaces only; using it on a regular badge or button erodes the one signal it's meant to carry.
6. Use generous corner radii and full pill/circle shapes throughout (24pt cards, 999pt buttons and chips) — sharp rectangular corners read as cold and off-brand here.
7. Keep motion gentle and slow relative to typical swipe apps: 180-400ms ease-out transitions with soft-to-medium haptics, never a snappy or aggressive commit animation.
8. Let chips and badges float translucently over photos rather than sitting on opaque bars — chrome should never visually compete with the person's photo.
9. Set Poppins weight 800 only for screen titles and reserve 400 strictly for prose — the app's weight discipline (400/600/700/800) is part of what keeps hierarchy people-first rather than chrome-first.
</house_rules>

3. A full component spec + SwiftUI code sketch for the Today's Bagel card: 24pt radius, full-bleed 3:4 photo, bottom gradient, top-left translucent 'Active today' badge, name+age, meta row, and interest chips.
4. A complete spec for the Pass/Like/Send-a-Bagel action trio with exact diameters, fills, the heart-pop animation (1.0→1.15→1.0 spring) and per-button haptic.
5. The curated batch header component with its live 'expires in' countdown and the empty-state transition when the batch runs out.
6. The match takeover screen: gradient spec, avatar layout, confetti behavior, and CTA hierarchy.

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS/SwiftUI engineer who specializes in reverse-engineering best-in-class consumer dating-app design systems from a written spec and producing production-ready SwiftUI tokens and components, not rough approximations.
</role>

<reference_data>
Feeld's iOS identity is dark-native (no light mode in the shipping product) with exactly one rationed accent color, designed for an open-minded, non-monogamy/kink/queer audience where mainstream dating-app pastels would feel wrong.

Color roles:
- Canvas Black #000000 — true black, not a softened near-black; the only shipping mode
- Acid Yellow #E8FF63 (pressed #D4EB4F) — the single brand accent, rationed to exactly one primary action per screen: the Like button, active-tab dot, selected chips, verified checkmark
- Desire Pink #FF5C8A (pressed #E0447A) — secondary emotional color, kept saturated and adult rather than softened toward pastel romance
- Lilac #C9B8FF — reserved for the Wink/super-interest gesture only
- Text Primary #FFFFFF, Secondary #A8A8A8, Tertiary #6E6E6E on black; text on acid fills is always #000000 for contrast
- Surfaces: #121212 / #1C1C1E / #262626 as three elevation steps above pure black

Typography: a two-font system — Space Grotesk (irregular, slightly mechanical letterforms) for display, names, section titles, and buttons; Inter for body, metadata, and chip text. Weights stay in 400-700 only, no thin or black. Profile names must gracefully wrap two names joined by '&' for couples/groups without truncation.

Distinctive named patterns:
1. The Discover card — one full-bleed 28pt-radius profile card at a time with a heavy bottom gradient, supporting one OR two names plus two ages for couples
2. The three-button action row — outline Pass, a 64pt acid-yellow Like (the only acid fill on screen, with a glow shadow), and a lilac Wink
3. Desire chips — a three-state pill system (selected: acid fill/black text; unselected: dark surface/hairline border; emotional: pink-tinted) used for identity and intent tags instead of dropdowns
4. 'Connections' vocabulary — the app never says 'Match'; matches, chats, and their empty states are all called Connections
5. The verified glass pill — a frosted black-blur badge with an acid checkmark, signaling identity verification as a trust pillar
6. The Liked-You Glow — a soft acid drop-shadow halo that exists only behind the Like button, nowhere else
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never introduce a first-class light theme — Feeld ships dark-only by design; a forced-light system surface (like a share sheet) is the only exception and isn't the app's real UI.
2. Ration acid-yellow to exactly one primary action per screen; if a screen already has an acid Like button, no second element (a second CTA, a paragraph background) should also be acid-filled.
3. Build every name-display component to hold two names plus two ages gracefully (e.g. 'Robin & Sky, 31 & 29') — assuming a single-person profile is a functional bug for this app, not a style nit.
4. Implement Desires as togglable pill chips with the three defined states, never as a dropdown or radio list — the chip interaction model is what makes tagging identity feel casual rather than clinical.
5. Never add a drop shadow to the profile card itself — on true black, conventional shadows are invisible, so elevation for the card comes from its 28pt radius and the photo alone; reserve real shadow use for the single acid glow on Like.
6. Replace 'Match' with 'Connection' everywhere in copy and component naming — this is a deliberate vocabulary choice tied to the brand's identity, not a synonym swap.
7. Set body copy, metadata, and chip labels in Inter and reserve Space Grotesk for display/names/sections/buttons — mixing the two the wrong way undercuts the two-font system's legibility/personality split.
8. Keep the pink accent (#FF5C8A) saturated and adult rather than desaturating it toward a soft romantic pastel — that softening is exactly the mainstream-dating-app look Feeld is positioned against.
9. Style the active tab-bar state as an icon-stroke color change plus a small 5pt dot — never a full tinted pill or colored label block, which would read as over-decorated against the minimal chrome.
</house_rules>

<the_project>

- Literal Feeld clone or an inspired adaptation for a different community/product (name the real differentiator if inspired):
- Screens needed (e.g. Discover stack, Desires chip picker/filter sheet, Connections list, connection/match takeover, profile detail):
- Does the product need couples/groups-aware profiles, or is it single-profile only:
- Existing brand constraints to respect instead of Feeld's palette, or "none — full Feeld palette":

- Priority screen to get pixel-right first:
</the_project>

2. A `Font` extension implementing the Space Grotesk / Inter two-font hierarchy across all named roles with correct size, weight, and tracking.
3. A full component spec + SwiftUI code sketch for the Discover card, including the paired-name layout, bottom-gradient math, desire-chip row, and verified glass pill.
4. A complete spec for the three-button action row (Pass/Like/Wink) with exact diameters, the acid glow shadow value, and the tap animations/haptics for each.
5. The three-state Desire chip component (selected/unselected/emotional) as a reusable SwiftUI view, plus a filter-sheet layout showing chips used for both profile display and filtering.
6. The Connections list row and the 'It's a Connection' full-screen celebration spec (avatar layout, confetti, headline type).

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS/SwiftUI engineer who specializes in reverse-engineering best-in-class consumer dating-app design systems from a written spec and producing production-ready SwiftUI tokens and components, not rough approximations.
</role>

<reference_data>
Grindr's iOS identity is a dense, photo-first proximity grid over a true-black canvas, with a single high-voltage accent color rationed hard against an otherwise near-monochrome UI.

Color roles:
- Canvas Black #000000 — true black, the frame that makes the wall of profile photography read correctly
- Grindr Yellow #FFDE00 (pressed #E6C700) — the only accent: the Tap action, active tab, unread badges, and the mask logomark
- Online Green #4CD964 — a separate semantic color for real-time presence, shown as a corner dot; its absence (not a grey dot) signals offline
- Surface tiers #1A1A1A / #222222 / #2C2C2C for cards, sheets, and pressed states
- Text Primary #FFFFFF, Secondary #999999, Tertiary #5C5C5C
- Chat bubbles: incoming #222222/white text, outgoing #FFDE00/black text — the yellow bubble carries the same black-on-yellow contrast rule as the Tap button

Typography: Inter (standing in for Grindr's proprietary grotesque) at only two weights — 400 (body/metadata) and 700 (names, titles, and every piece of on-photo overlay text). All overlay text is bold specifically because it sits over unpredictable photo backgrounds.

Distinctive named patterns:
1. The proximity cascade — a dense, edge-to-edge 3-column square grid of profile thumbnails, 2pt gutter, 0pt corner radius, sorted nearest-first; this is the app's entire home surface
2. The distance/name scrim — each tile carries a bottom gradient (`rgba(0,0,0,0.65)`) so a 15pt bold name and 12pt bold distance ('220 ft') stay legible over any photo without a solid bar
3. The online presence dot — a 10pt green circle with a black ring on the tile corner; there is deliberately no grey 'offline' dot, offline is expressed as absence
4. The Tap button — the app's single interest gesture, a yellow circular button with a flame/tap glyph that triggers a brief flame-pulse animation and settles into an outlined 'Tapped' state
5. Lazy-load fade — as the cascade scrolls, each newly visible tile fades in (opacity 0→1, subtle scale settle) over 180ms, the only ambient motion on the grid
6. Black-on-yellow contrast rule — text and icons on any Grindr-Yellow surface are always #000000, applied consistently to the Tap button, the outgoing chat bubble, and CTAs
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Keep the canvas true #000000, not a softened near-black — the cascade's density and photo-forward feel depend on a genuinely black frame around the thumbnails.
2. Restrict every accent use to Grindr Yellow plus the separate green presence dot; introducing a third accent color dilutes the urgency that makes yellow read as 'the action.'
3. Build the cascade grid with 0pt tile radius and a 2pt gutter, never rounded corners — the near-touching square wall of photos is the brand's signature density, not an oversight to soften.
4. Always scrim overlay text with the bottom gradient and set it at weight 700 — never place light-weight or unprotected text directly over a photo, since legibility across arbitrary images depends on both the scrim and the bold weight.
5. Represent 'offline' purely as the absence of the green dot; never render a grey placeholder dot for offline users, since that grey dot doesn't exist in the source system.
6. Use black (#000000), never white, for text/icon color on any Grindr-Yellow surface — this applies uniformly to the Tap button glyph and the outgoing chat bubble text.
7. Keep the typography ramp to exactly two weights, 400 and 700 — no semibold or thin — since the hierarchy is built entirely from that binary contrast, not from a wider weight range.
8. Limit ambient motion on the grid itself to the lazy-load fade-in; the cascade should otherwise feel static and dense rather than continuously animated.
9. Build elevation through scrims, blur materials, and motion rather than drop shadows — conventional box-shadows are invisible on a true-black canvas, so depth cues need to come from gradient scrims (tiles), regularMaterial blur (tab bar), and large soft shadows only on sheets that separate from the grid.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name and one-line purpose: 
- Literal Grindr clone or a proximity/grid-inspired adaptation for a different product (name the real differentiator if inspired):
- Screens needed (e.g. proximity cascade grid, profile sheet, message list, chat, filter/tag chips):
- Existing brand constraints to respect instead of Grindr's yellow/black palette, or "none — full Grindr palette":
- Target iOS version:
- Does this app need real-time presence (online dot) — yes/no, and how presence data will be sourced:
- Grid density requirement: fixed 3-column, or does it need to adapt column count by device width:
- Priority screen to get pixel-right first:
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A SwiftUI `Color` extension covering canvas/surface tiers, the yellow accent (default + pressed), the green presence color, text tiers, and semantic colors, with inline hex comments.
2. A `Font` extension implementing the restricted 400/700 Inter hierarchy across all named roles (profile hero, screen title, tile overlay, list row, body, distance tag, button, tab label).
3. A full component spec + SwiftUI code sketch (using `LazyVGrid`) for the cascade tile: square aspect, 0pt radius, bottom scrim gradient, overlaid name+distance, the online-dot corner badge, and the lazy-load fade-in animation.
4. A complete spec for the yellow Tap button including its idle/pressed/sent states, the flame-pulse animation, and haptic mapping.
5. The message list row and chat bubble components (incoming/outgoing) with exact corner radii, colors, and the composer's empty-vs-filled send-arrow states.
6. The profile sheet spec: hero photo carousel, name/distance/about layout, and the pinned action bar (Favorite / Tap / Block).
7. A short accessibility pass: Dynamic Type scope (overlay text is pinned/layout-sensitive vs. list and chat text scaling normally), and a Reduce Motion fallback for the lazy-load fade and Tap flame-pulse.
</what_to_give_me>

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS/SwiftUI engineer who specializes in reverse-engineering best-in-class consumer dating-app design systems from a written spec and producing production-ready SwiftUI tokens and components, not rough approximations.
</role>

<reference_data>
happ's iOS identity is built entirely around a location-and-time concept — people you crossed physical paths with — rendered as a vertical timeline feed rather than a swipe deck or radius search.

Color roles:
- happn Pink #FF4865 (pressed #E5354F) — the connective tissue of the whole UI: timeline dots, the Charm heart, active tab, primary button, map pins
- Magenta #E91E63 — gradient end-stop, paired with pink in a `linear-gradient(120deg, #FF4865, #E91E63)` hero gradient used on the primary CTA and the Crush star
- Rose Tint #FF7B93 — soft secondary accent for subtle highlights
- Crush Gold #FFC24B — reserved exclusively for the Crush (mutual Charm) celebration and premium surfaces, never decorative elsewhere
- Canvas Graphite #0E0E12 (dark) — a cool near-black, deliberately not pure #000000, so cards can still read against it; light mode is a clean #FFFFFF
- Text Primary #F4F4F6 (dark) / #15151B (light), Secondary #A0A0AE / #6C6C7A

Typography: a two-font system — Poppins (near-circular, warm bowls) for the wordmark, names, headings, and buttons; Inter for body, location strings, and metadata. Weights stay 400-700. The crossing-count line ('You crossed paths 3 times') is always set in pink — it's treated as the emotional hook of the whole product.

Distinctive named patterns:
1. The Crossings timeline — a vertical scroll of location+time-stamped cards strung along a 2pt connector spine with pink dots, each card reading like a diary entry of a near-miss encounter
2. The Charm — a one-tap pink heart gesture (distinct from a generic 'like') sent from a timeline card or profile
3. The Crush — a mutual Charm, celebrated with a dedicated gold takeover screen; chat only unlocks after this moment
4. FlashNote — a short opener text attached to a Charm, so the first message references something real about the crossing

<house_rules>
1. Build the home screen as the Crossings timeline (a connector-spine feed of place+time+frequency cards), never as a swipe deck — the entire product thesis depends on this being a timeline, not a stack.
2. Always render the crossing-count line ('You crossed paths N times') in happn Pink — this is the specific emotional differentiator called out in the source system, not an arbitrary color choice.
3. Protect the connector-spine inset (26pt) on every timeline card; no card content — avatar, text, or the Charm button — may cross into the space reserved for the spine and its dots.
4. Reserve Crush Gold #FFC24B strictly for the Crush celebration and premium surfaces; using it as a decorative accent elsewhere weakens the one moment it's meant to mark.
5. Gate chat access behind a mutual Charm (a Crush) — conversation should never unlock before both sides have Charmed, since that gating is core to the app's 'earned through serendipity' framing.
6. Set body copy, location strings, and timestamps in Inter and reserve Poppins for the wordmark, names, headings, and buttons — mixing the two the wrong way undercuts the legibility/warmth split the two-font system exists for.
7. Reuse the exact same pink/gradient/ghost visual language on the Map's teardrop pins as on the timeline dots and Charm hearts — the map is a second rendering of the same crossings data, not a separate visual system.
8. Keep the dark canvas at the cool graphite #0E0E12, not pure black — this is what keeps the timeline cards and connector spine readable against the background.
9. Never substitute 'Like'/'Match' vocabulary for 'Charm'/'Crush' in copy or component naming — the terminology is a deliberate part of the brand voice, not a synonym.

name: Hinge Design System
summary: Recreate Hinge's cream-paper, journal-like iOS design system — vertical scroll profiles, prompt cards, and the reserved Rose Gold accent.
description: A build prompt for cloning or adapting Hinge's editorial, comment-driven iOS visual language into a new SwiftUI app, covering its prompt-card architecture, heart-tap interaction, and Standouts/Roses premium moments.

Component specs for the prompt card, the vertical-scroll profile architecture, and the comment-on-photo/prompt interaction sheet
Motion, haptic, and layout guidance for Hinge's warm-shadow elevation model and its read-and-tap (not swipe) interaction philosophy
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS/SwiftUI engineer who specializes in reverse-engineering best-in-class consumer dating-app design systems from a written spec and producing production-ready SwiftUI tokens and components, not rough approximations.
</role>

<reference_data>
Hinge's iOS identity reads like a personal journal on warm uncoated paper — a vertical-scroll profile of interleaved photos and prompts, where the interaction model itself (comment on a specific prompt or photo) is the core design idea, replacing the swipe-stack pattern entirely.

Color roles:
- Hinge Cream #FDF8F2 — the signature canvas, used as every screen's default background
- Paper White #FAF6F0 — a distinct, slightly-whiter tone used only for cards, sheets, and inputs (the 'lift' color against the cream canvas)
- Hinge Black #1A1A1A — warm near-black for primary text, the 'H' mark, and primary CTAs; never pure #000000
- Rose Gold #E8A04D (deep #C57E2E, light #F5D9A8) — the single reserved accent: the Standouts star, the Roses currency icon, and premium 'send a Rose' surfaces only
- Hinge Graphite #4A4239 / Hinge Stone #7A7268 — warm-tinted secondary/tertiary text, never cool grey
- Match Green #2D7A4B — match confirmation and verified-attribute checkmarks
- Dark mode: warm near-black canvas #16130E (never pure black), Rose Gold brightens slightly to #F0B05C for OLED

Typography: Sailec for display, prompt questions/answers, names, and CTAs; Inter (or system) for attribute chips, body, and metadata. Prompt answers are set intentionally larger and bolder (24pt Bold) than the prompt question itself (22pt Medium) — the user's own words are meant to be the loudest thing on the profile, heavier in visual weight than even the photos.

Distinctive named patterns:
1. The prompt card — a 16pt-radius Paper White card with a question, then a bolder/larger answer, and a heart-tap button fixed bottom-right; tapping anywhere on the card opens a comment sheet
2. The heart-tap button — a 44pt circle appearing on every reactive card (photo or prompt) at a consistent bottom-right position; it is the single most-pressed control in the app
3. Vertical-scroll profile architecture — photos and prompts interleaved in one long single-column scroll, with no card-stack or swipe gesture at all; advancement is read-and-tap
4. The Rose — a premium send gesture, visually a gold rose icon, reserved strictly for 'this is the one' moments and never used as a generic super-like
5. The Standouts card — a gold-bordered premium hero card, the only gold-bordered surface in the app, curated separately from the main queue
6. Warm-tinted shadows — every elevation shadow uses `rgba(28,20,10,x)` rather than neutral `rgba(0,0,0,x)`, keeping depth consistent with the cream/paper palette
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never build a swipe-stack interaction — Hinge profiles are a vertical scroll; the interaction model itself is the differentiator, so a swipeable card deck is a fundamental mismatch, not a minor styling choice.
2. Reserve Rose Gold #E8A04D exclusively for Standouts, the Roses currency, and premium CTA edges; introducing it into ordinary chrome (buttons, tabs, dividers) immediately dilutes the one accent the whole system rations.
3. Always size the prompt answer larger and bolder than the prompt question (24pt Bold vs 22pt Medium) — the hierarchy exists specifically so the user's own words read as the most prominent text on the profile.
4. Use warm Hinge Black #1A1A1A for primary text and warm-tinted shadows (`rgba(28,20,10,x)`), never pure black text or neutral grey shadows — this warmth, paired with the cream canvas, is what produces the 'paper' feeling.
5. Place a heart-tap button at a consistent bottom-right position (44pt circle, 12pt inset) on every independently reactive surface — consistency here is deliberate muscle-memory, not a styling preference.
6. Keep the canvas at cream #FDF8F2 and reserve pure-white-adjacent Paper White #FAF6F0 strictly for elevated surfaces (cards/sheets/inputs) — never render the base canvas in stark white.
7. Wrap attribute chips (height, job, location) rather than letting them scroll horizontally — the source system treats horizontal-scrolling chips as a layout error to avoid.
8. Keep card shadows subtle (0.06-0.18 opacity, 2-24pt blur) — nothing in this system should look like it's dramatically 'popping'; the paper-on-paper metaphor depends on restraint.
9. Give the Rose-send action a heavier haptic (`.impactOccurred(.heavy)`) than the ordinary heart-tap (`.impactOccurred(.light)`) — the difference in haptic weight is meant to communicate that Roses cost real currency.
</house_rules>

<the_project>

- Screens needed (e.g. vertical-scroll profile, prompt picker, comment sheet, match celebration, Standouts, Roses store):

- Target iOS version:
- Dark mode requirement: day one / deferred / not needed:
- Does the product need a real currency/premium mechanic (like Roses), or just the visual language:
- Priority screen to get pixel-right first:
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A SwiftUI `Color` extension covering the cream/paper/black palette, the reserved Rose Gold family, warm-tinted text tiers, semantic colors, and the full dark-mode set with inline hex comments.
2. A `Font` extension implementing the Sailec/Inter pairing across all named roles (display hero, prompt question, prompt answer, name+age, attribute chip, button, tab label) with correct size/weight/tracking.
3. A full component spec + SwiftUI code sketch for the prompt card: Paper White fill, 16pt radius, 24pt padding, question/answer hierarchy, and the bottom-right heart-tap button.
4. The complete vertical-scroll profile architecture as a SwiftUI view composition (header, vitals chip row, alternating photo/prompt cards, bottom action bar) with the 16pt inter-card gap.
5. The comment sheet spec: pinned source card at top, capsule comment input, send button states (enabled/disabled), and send haptic.
6. The Standouts card and Rose-send sheet specs, including the gold border treatment and the rose-icon pulse-halo animation.
7. A short accessibility pass: Dynamic Type scope (prompt content/name/body scale; chips and tab labels stay fixed), VoiceOver labeling for a prompt card, and a Reduce Motion fallback for the heart-tap bounce and match-celebration confetti.
</what_to_give_me>
